<a name="pkg-functions"></a>
## Functions

<a name="DXF"></a>
### func DXF

<pre>func DXF(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, w io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer">Writer</a>, body *decad.<a href="decad.md#Body">Body</a>, tol units.Value, view <a href="#DrawingView">DrawingView</a>, opts ...decad.<a href="decad.md#TessellateOption">TessellateOption</a>) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

DXF writes a 2D drawing of body as an ASCII DXF file, release 12, at the
requested chord tolerance (agent-docs/dxf-export-design.md). The drawing is an
orthographic projection along view: every feature edge of the body's
tessellation becomes LINE entities in millimetres at full scale, on the
VISIBLE layer where a surface does not hide it and on the dashed HIDDEN layer
where one does. A feature edge is a boundary or non-manifold edge, a crease of
more than 30 degrees, or a silhouette; a curved face is drawn as the chords
of its tessellation, so a circle is a polygon. No dimensions, text, hatching
or title block are drawn.

The mesh defaults to decad.VerifyNone; pass decad.WithVerification to demand
stronger proofs. Hidden-line removal reads a 2048-pixel depth buffer, so an
edge passing behind a surface by less than a few pixels of the drawing's size
reads as visible. ctx, w and body MUST NOT be nil, and view MUST have a
direction and an up vector not parallel to it, each otherwise
decad.ErrDegenerate.

<a name="DXFSection"></a>
### func DXFSection

<pre>func DXFSection(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, w io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer">Writer</a>, body *decad.<a href="decad.md#Body">Body</a>, plane r3.Frame, tol units.Value, hatch <a href="#DXFHatch">DXFHatch</a>) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

DXFSection writes the cut of body by plane as an ASCII DXF file, release 12,
with the cut hatched, as a section view of an engineering drawing
(agent-docs/dxf-export-design.md §10). The drawing's X and Y axes are the
plane's U and V in millimetres at full scale, from the plane's origin. The
outlines of the cut, read from [decad.Body.SectionOutline](<decad.md#Body.SectionOutline>), are LINE entities
on the SECTION layer, and the material between them is filled by parallel LINE
entities on the HATCH layer: a hole inside an outline is left empty, and the
lines lie at whole multiples of the spacing across their direction, so two
sections hatched alike carry one family of lines.

The outline is the cut of the body's tessellation at tol, a reading of the
mesh as SectionOutline says, so a curved wall is drawn as chords. A plane that
misses the body writes a file with no entities. ctx, w and body MUST NOT be
nil and plane MUST be valid, each otherwise decad.ErrDegenerate. Spacing MUST
be positive: a zero is decad.ErrDegenerate, a negative value
decad.ErrNegativeMagnitude and a wrong unit kind decad.ErrUnitKind, as is the
wrong unit kind for Angle. A spacing so fine that the cut needs over 100000
lines is decad.ErrDegenerate. Every failure writes nothing. The tessellation
options of [decad.Body.SectionOutline](<decad.md#Body.SectionOutline>) are not offered: it verifies the
mesh's boundary itself.

<a name="DXFSheet"></a>
### func DXFSheet

<pre>func DXFSheet(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, w io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer">Writer</a>, body *decad.<a href="decad.md#Body">Body</a>, tol units.Value, paper <a href="#DXFPaper">DXFPaper</a>, opts ...decad.<a href="decad.md#TessellateOption">TessellateOption</a>) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

DXFSheet writes several views of body at a stated scale on a sheet of stated
paper size, inside a border with a title block, as an ASCII DXF file
(agent-docs/dxf-export-design.md §6). Coordinates are paper millimetres, the
paper's lower left corner at the origin. Each view is drawn as [DXF](<#DXF>) draws it
and then scaled and placed; the row of views is centred in the area above the
title block, and when paper.Dimensions is set each view carries its overall
width and height.

The mesh defaults to decad.VerifyNone; pass decad.WithVerification to demand
stronger proofs. ctx, w and body MUST NOT be nil and paper.Views must hold a
view valid as for [DXF](<#DXF>), otherwise decad.ErrDegenerate. Width, Height, Scale
must be positive: a zero is decad.ErrDegenerate, a negative value
decad.ErrNegativeMagnitude and a wrong unit kind decad.ErrUnitKind, and Margin
and Gap must not be negative. A title with a character other than printable
ASCII, and views that do not fit the paper with their dimensions, are
decad.ErrDegenerate; a sheet that is too small writes nothing.

<a name="DXFViews"></a>
### func DXFViews

<pre>func DXFViews(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, w io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer">Writer</a>, body *decad.<a href="decad.md#Body">Body</a>, tol units.Value, views []<a href="#DrawingView">DrawingView</a>, gap units.Value, opts ...decad.<a href="decad.md#TessellateOption">TessellateOption</a>) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

DXFViews writes several views of body on one DXF sheet, laid out in a row
(agent-docs/dxf-export-design.md §5). Each view is drawn as [DXF](<#DXF>) draws it, then
moved so that its lower left corner sits on the sheet's baseline: the first
view's left edge is at x = 0, and each later view starts gap to the right of the
one before. The views share the VISIBLE and HIDDEN layers. Coordinates are
millimetres at full scale.

The mesh defaults to decad.VerifyNone; pass decad.WithVerification to demand
stronger proofs. ctx, w and body MUST NOT be nil, and views MUST hold at least
one view, each valid as for [DXF](<#DXF>), otherwise decad.ErrDegenerate. gap is a
non-negative length: a negative gap is decad.ErrNegativeMagnitude and a wrong
unit kind decad.ErrUnitKind.

<a name="GCodePerimeters"></a>
### func GCodePerimeters

<pre>func GCodePerimeters(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, w io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer">Writer</a>, body *decad.<a href="decad.md#Body">Body</a>, tol units.Value, spec <a href="#GCodeSpec">GCodeSpec</a>) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

GCodePerimeters writes the toolpath that prints body's outline layer by layer as G-code
(agent-docs/gcode-design.md): the perimeter of each layer, traced once along the body's section at the
middle of the layer, a hole traced as well, and, when the spec sets InfillSpacing, rectilinear infill
inside the perimeters, its lines alternating between the X and Y directions from one layer to the next. The
first and last SolidLayers layers are filled solid, their lines a line width apart, and PerimeterInset moves
each perimeter half a line width into the material. It is the first stage of a slicer, with no skin found
from what lies above or below, or support, and it answers whether a print would stand: each layer's line is where the part's outline is.

The file uses millimetres, absolute positioning and absolute extrusion (G21, G90, M82). The bed is
the plane z = 0 of the world and the print starts at the body's lowest point, so layer i is
printed at z = zmin + (i+1)·LayerHeight, and there are floor((zmax − zmin)/LayerHeight) layers, the
part above the last whole layer left unprinted. Each loop of the section is a travel move to its
first point at the layer's height, then extruding moves round it and back to the start. The
extrusion for a move is its length times the line's cross-section, LayerHeight·LineWidth, divided
by the filament's cross-section. The outline is the cut of the body's tessellation at tol, a reading of
the mesh as [decad.Body.SectionOutline](<decad.md#Body.SectionOutline>) says, so a curved wall is printed as chords.

ctx, w and body MUST NOT be nil, each otherwise decad.ErrDegenerate. A length of the spec MUST be
positive (zero is decad.ErrDegenerate, a negative value decad.ErrNegativeMagnitude, a wrong kind
decad.ErrUnitKind), as the feed rate (a velocity); a body lower than one layer, or one needing over
100000 layers, is decad.ErrDegenerate. Every failure writes nothing.

<a name="GLTF"></a>
### func GLTF

<pre>func GLTF(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, w io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer">Writer</a>, body *decad.<a href="decad.md#Body">Body</a>, tol units.Value, opts ...decad.<a href="decad.md#TessellateOption">TessellateOption</a>) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

GLTF writes body as a deterministic glTF 2.0 file at the requested chord
tolerance: one JSON document whose single buffer is embedded as a base64
data URI (agent-docs/gltf-export-design.md). The file holds one scene, one
node, one mesh and one triangle primitive, with positions and 32-bit indices
and no normals, materials or textures. Positions are in metres, as glTF
requires, so every millimetre coordinate is multiplied by 0.001 and stored as
a 32-bit float, and no axis is exchanged: decad's +Z stays +Z.

The mesh defaults to decad.VerifyNone; pass decad.WithVerification to demand
stronger proofs. A sheet writes an open mesh. ctx, w and body MUST NOT be
nil, and tol is a positive length.

<a name="IGES"></a>
### func IGES

<pre>func IGES(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, w io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer">Writer</a>, body *decad.<a href="decad.md#Body">Body</a>, tol units.Value) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

IGES writes body as an IGES 5.3 file of manifold solid B-reps (agent-docs/iges-export-design.md): the verified
tessellation at tol, one planar face per triangle, so any solid the evaluator can tessellate is written as the
planar solid ReadIGES reads, and a read back mesh has the body's own triangles. A body of several lumps writes
one solid per lump and a cavity a void shell of its solid. The file is millimetres with a model space scale of 1.

ctx, w and body MUST NOT be nil, each otherwise decad.ErrDegenerate. A body that is not a valid solid is
decad.ErrNotSolid, a mesh whose boundary is not verified, whose edges are not each used twice or that does not map
to the body's shells is decad.ErrUnsupported, and a failure writes nothing.

<a name="NewSTEPFile"></a>
### func NewSTEPFile

<pre>func NewSTEPFile(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, body *decad.<a href="decad.md#Body">Body</a>, tol units.Value, header step.Header) (step.File, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

NewSTEPFile builds an AP214 file from one boundary-verified solid.
tol is Body.Tessellate's chord tolerance. The caller supplies the mandatory
header fields, including a timestamp; AP214's schema replaces Header.Schemas.
Supported plane, cylinder, cone, sphere and torus boundaries retain analytic
faces, lines, circles and ellipses. Other boundaries use one planar ADVANCED\_FACE per mesh triangle.
A solid with cavities writes a BREP\_WITH\_VOIDS: the outer shell and each void
shell as an ORIENTED\_CLOSED\_SHELL, all as planar faces per mesh triangle
(agent-docs/step-export-design.md §9). A body of several lumps writes one
solid per lump, all as items of one representation. A sheet is refused. ctx and body must not be nil.

<a name="PNG"></a>
### func PNG

<pre>func PNG(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, w io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer">Writer</a>, body *decad.<a href="decad.md#Body">Body</a>, tol units.Value, view <a href="#View">View</a>, opts ...decad.<a href="decad.md#TessellateOption">TessellateOption</a>) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

PNG draws body as a PNG image of its tessellation at the requested chord
tolerance, so a program can look at a part (agent-docs/png-export-design.md).
The camera is orthographic and the model is centred and scaled to fill the
image with a margin, keeping its proportions. A face is lit by a headlight on
the camera and shaded flat by how squarely it faces it: a face turned to the
camera is light blue, shaded toward 30% as it turns edge on. A face that looks
away from the camera, which shows where a sheet is open or a mesh is wound
inside out, is orange. A pixel no face covers is opaque white. No outlines,
axes or labels are drawn.

The mesh defaults to decad.VerifyNone; pass decad.WithVerification to demand
stronger proofs. The output is deterministic for a platform: equal body,
tolerance, view and options give equal bytes. ctx, w and body MUST NOT be nil,
and view MUST have a direction, an up vector not parallel to it and sides in
range, each otherwise decad.ErrDegenerate.

<a name="PNGBodies"></a>
### func PNGBodies

<pre>func PNGBodies(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, w io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer">Writer</a>, bodies []*decad.<a href="decad.md#Body">Body</a>, tol units.Value, view <a href="#View">View</a>, opts ...decad.<a href="decad.md#TessellateOption">TessellateOption</a>) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

PNGBodies draws several bodies in one PNG image, as [PNG](<#PNG>) draws one
(agent-docs/png-export-design.md §5). Each body is tessellated at the chord
tolerance and the meshes are drawn together, so a nearer body hides a farther
one and the whole scene is centred and scaled to fill the image with the
margin [PNG](<#PNG>) leaves. A face toward the camera is blue and one looking away is
orange, unless [View](<#View>).Colors gives each body its own colour for the faces that
look toward the camera. A pixel no face covers is
opaque white.

The meshes default to decad.VerifyNone; pass decad.WithVerification to demand
stronger proofs. The output is deterministic for a platform: equal bodies in
equal order, tolerance, view and options give equal bytes. ctx and w MUST NOT
be nil, bodies MUST hold at least one body and no nil, and view is valid as
for [PNG](<#PNG>), each otherwise decad.ErrDegenerate.

<a name="STEP"></a>
### func STEP

<pre>func STEP(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, w io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer">Writer</a>, body *decad.<a href="decad.md#Body">Body</a>, tol units.Value, opts ...<a href="#STEPOption">STEPOption</a>) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

STEP writes one AP214 file. Supply the name, author, and organization
as options, or use WithSTEPHeader for a complete step.Header. When no
timestamp option is supplied, STEP uses the current UTC time.
Geometry and references are built before the writer is touched. Invalid
header data also leaves the writer untouched. An I/O error may leave a
partial file. ctx, w, and body must not be nil.

<a name="STL"></a>
### func STL

<pre>func STL(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, w io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer">Writer</a>, body *decad.<a href="decad.md#Body">Body</a>, tol units.Value, opts ...decad.<a href="decad.md#TessellateOption">TessellateOption</a>) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

STL writes body as deterministic ASCII STL at the requested chord tolerance.
The mesh defaults to decad.VerifyNone; pass decad.WithVerification to demand
stronger proofs. A sheet produces an open STL file even though STL uses the

<a name="ThreeMF"></a>
### func ThreeMF

<pre>func ThreeMF(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, w io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer">Writer</a>, body *decad.<a href="decad.md#Body">Body</a>, tol units.Value, opts ...decad.<a href="decad.md#TessellateOption">TessellateOption</a>) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

ThreeMF writes one body as a deterministic 3MF Core package at the requested
chord tolerance. Solids become model objects; sheets become surface objects.
The mesh defaults to decad.VerifyNone. Pass decad.WithVerification to request
stronger proofs. ctx, w, and body must not be nil.

<a name="ThreeMFItems"></a>
### func ThreeMFItems

<pre>func ThreeMFItems(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, w io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer">Writer</a>, items []<a href="#ThreeMFItem">ThreeMFItem</a>, tol units.Value,
    opts ...decad.<a href="decad.md#TessellateOption">TessellateOption</a>) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

ThreeMFItems writes several bodies as one deterministic 3MF Core package: one
named object and one build item each, vertices moved by the item's
Placement. A body named by several items is tessellated once. A Placement
that reflects, or is not a valid transform, is decad.ErrDegenerate, because a
reflection would turn the mesh inside out. An empty item list, or a nil body,
is decad.ErrDegenerate. The writer's other rules are ThreeMF's. ctx and w
must not be nil.

<a name="DXFPaper"></a>
### type DXFPaper

<pre>type DXFPaper struct {
    // Views are laid in a row, left to right, in the order given.

    Scale units.Value

    // as &#34;LABEL: value&#34;. Up to three stack in one column; more fill a second
    // column and each then holds at most 24 characters
    // (agent-docs/dxf-export-design.md §9).
    Fields []<a href="#DXFField">DXFField</a>
    // Dimensions adds, for each view, its overall width below it and its overall
    // height left of it, as the model&#39;s true size and not the drawn one, and the
    // diameter of each whole circle and the radius of each whole arc the view draws
    // as one (agent-docs/dxf-export-design.md §8).
    Dimensions <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a>
    // CentreLines marks the centre of each whole circle and arc a view draws as one with a cross of two chain-dashed
    // lines on the CENTRE layer: a circle&#39;s reaching 2 mm past its edge, an arc&#39;s 3 mm across
    // (agent-docs/dxf-export-design.md §11).
    CentreLines <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a>
}</pre>

DXFPaper describes a drawing sheet for [DXFSheet](<#DXFSheet>): its paper size, the scale
of the views on it, a border with a title block, and optionally the overall
size of each view as a dimension.

<a name="DrawingView"></a>
### type DrawingView

<pre>type DrawingView struct {
    Direction, Up r3.Vec
}</pre>

DrawingView is the direction a drawing looks along. Direction is the way the
camera looks, from the eye into the scene, and Up sets the drawing's vertical;
neither need be a unit vector. The drawing's X axis is Direction × Up and its
Y axis is up the sheet.

<a name="IsometricDrawingView"></a>
#### func IsometricDrawingView

<pre>func IsometricDrawingView() <a href="#DrawingView">DrawingView</a></pre>

IsometricDrawingView looks along (-1, -1, -1) with +Z up the sheet, as
[IsometricView](<#IsometricView>) does.

<a name="GCodeSpec"></a>
### type GCodeSpec

<pre>type GCodeSpec struct {
    // LayerHeight is the thickness of a layer.
    LayerHeight units.Value
    // LineWidth is the width of the extruded line, the nozzle&#39;s.
    LineWidth units.Value
    // FilamentDiameter is the diameter of the filament the extruder feeds, 1.75 mm for the common one.
    FilamentDiameter units.Value
    // FeedRate is the speed along an extruding move.
    FeedRate units.Value
    // InfillSpacing is the distance between the lines of rectilinear infill, a positive length. The zero value
    // writes none, and a layer is its perimeters alone.
    InfillSpacing units.Value
    // SolidLayers is the number of layers at the bottom and at the top of the print that are filled solid, with
    // lines a line width apart, whatever the InfillSpacing. The zero value makes none, and a negative one is
    // decad.ErrDegenerate.
    SolidLayers <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
    // PerimeterInset moves each perimeter half a line width into the material, so that the printed line&#39;s edge and
    // not its middle lies on the body&#39;s outline (agent-docs/gcode-design.md G10). The infill is unchanged.
    PerimeterInset <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a>
    // Retraction is the length of filament pulled back before each travel move between two extruded lines and pushed
    // forward again after it, a positive length. The zero value writes no retraction. The first travel of the print,
    // which follows no extrusion, has none.
    Retraction units.Value
    // NozzleTemperature and BedTemperature, when set, heat the nozzle and the bed to that temperature, waiting for it,
    // before the first layer, and turn both off after the last. A temperature is positive in degrees Celsius and below
    // 1000 degrees, and the zero values leave the heaters alone.
    NozzleTemperature, BedTemperature units.AffineValue
    // StartCode and EndCode are lines written as they are after the header and the heating, and after the last layer:
    // the machine&#39;s own start and end sequence. A line break in them starts a line of the file.
    StartCode, EndCode <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>
    // FanSpeed, a dimensionless fraction above 0 and at most 1, turns the part cooling fan on at that share of its full
    // speed (M106) at the start of layer FanFromLayer, counted from zero, and off (M107) after the last layer. The zero
    // value leaves the fan alone. FanFromLayer is from 0 to one less than the number of layers.
    FanSpeed     units.Value
    FanFromLayer <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
    // Skirt is the number of loops traced round the part in the first layer before its perimeters, from the one nearest
    // the part outward, each a line width outside the last (agent-docs/gcode-design.md G16). SkirtDistance is the gap from
    // the part&#39;s outline to the first loop, a positive length that Skirt requires. The zero Skirt writes none, and a
    // negative one is decad.ErrDegenerate.
    Skirt         <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
    SkirtDistance units.Value
}</pre>

GCodeSpec describes the print GCodePerimeters writes G-code for. LayerHeight, LineWidth and
FilamentDiameter are positive lengths, and FeedRate a positive velocity.

<a name="View"></a>
### type View

<pre>type View struct {
    Direction, Up r3.Vec
    Width, Height <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
    Outlines      <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a>
    FieldOfView   units.Value
    // Colors, when not empty, are the colours of the bodies&#39; faces that look
    // toward the camera, one for each body drawn, in order: [PNG] and [MeshPNG]
    // draw one body and so take one, and [PNGBodies] takes one for each body.
    // The alpha channel is ignored. Faces that look away stay orange.
    Colors []color.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/image/color#RGBA">RGBA</a>
    // HiddenEdges draws the feature edges behind surfaces as dashed light grey
    // lines under the outlines (agent-docs/png-export-design.md §9).
    HiddenEdges <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a>
    // Shadows casts the key light&#39;s shadows: a face a nearer one hides from the
    // light is drawn at the ambient level (agent-docs/png-export-design.md §10).
    Shadows <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a>
    // ShadowSoftness, an angle, makes the shadows soft: it is the angular radius of
    // the key light, which is sampled over a disc of that radius so a shadow grades from
    // dark to light across a penumbra that widens with the distance from the occluder
    // (agent-docs/png-export-design.md §14). The zero units.Value is a point light with hard
    // shadows. It needs Shadows, and is at most 45 degrees.
    ShadowSoftness units.Value
    // Gloss, dimensionless from 0 to 1, gives the lit faces a specular highlight of that strength: white added
    // where a face turns the key light toward the camera (agent-docs/png-export-design.md §15). The zero
    // units.Value is matte; shadows are as dark as without it.
    Gloss units.Value
    // BackColor, when set, is the colour of the faces that look away from the
    // camera, in place of orange: they show where a sheet is open or a mesh is
    // wound inside out, and a part&#39;s far side through an open shell. Its alpha is
    // ignored (agent-docs/png-export-design.md §11).
    BackColor *color.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/image/color#RGBA">RGBA</a>
    // Opacity, when not empty, is how opaque each body is, one dimensionless value from above 0 to 1 for each body
    // drawn, in order as Colors is: 1 is solid and less lets what lies behind show through, the body&#39;s own far side
    // included (agent-docs/png-export-design.md §16). A view whose bodies are all solid is the same as one with
    // no Opacity. It does not combine with Shadows.
    Opacity []units.Value
}</pre>

View is an orthographic camera and the size of the image it draws
(agent-docs/png-export-design.md). Direction is the way the camera looks,
from the eye into the scene, and Up sets the image's vertical. Neither need
be a unit vector. The image's right is Direction × Up. Width and Height are
pixels, each from 16 to 8192. Colors gives each body its own colour
(agent-docs/png-export-design.md §8).

Outlines draws the body's visible feature edges over the shading, one dark
pixel wide (agent-docs/png-export-design.md §6). FieldOfView, an angle, makes
the camera perspective with that field of view across the smaller image side
of the scene's bounding sphere; the zero units.Value is the orthographic camera
(agent-docs/png-export-design.md §7). Outlines, HiddenEdges and Shadows take the perspective
camera too (agent-docs/png-export-design.md §12).

<a name="IsometricView"></a>
#### func IsometricView

<pre>func IsometricView(width, height <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>) <a href="#View">View</a></pre>

IsometricView looks at the model along the diagonal from above its +X, +Y,
\+Z corner, with +Z up the image, so the model's top, front and right faces
show. It draws width by height pixels.
